Synopsis:
Ide mainly talks about the interaction the player can have with Rolan in his dialog (HAV_ProdigyLament_Rolan), where he berates the kid for not giving him more alcohol. This dialog continues that narrative beat, and players can acquire a book Ide was planning to give Rolan.

Cluster Contexts:
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Ide.json: Ide and Rolan recently had a falling-out after an incident in which Rolan drank heavily (three bottles) and snapped at Ide; Ide is hurt, frustrated, and avoiding eye contact. Off-screen, Ide had found an old, probably magical book he intended to give Rolan so the boy could learn spells instead of numbing himself, but Ide is now reluctant to hand it over. The player can continue this beat by consoling Ide, pressing for the book, or offering to deliver it to Rolan on Ide’s behalf. The samples show Ide is protective and awkwardly grateful—he admits Rolan saved them previously—so the conflict is more personal than purely practical.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Rolan.json: Rolan is an apprentice wizard whose siblings were recently captured by cultists. He's stuck in a tavern in the middle of the cursed lands where they were taken, drinking heavily, blaming himself for their loss. When he sees the players, he turns his frustration onto them - he's only here because they convinced him to stay with the other tieflings who were captured in the first place.Rolan is in fact the only reason any of the tieflings are still alive, having protected them from the traitorous Zevlor, who planned to give them over to the cult. He doesn't feel like a hero though - he feels like a failure.
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_Rolan.json: Dialog with Sorcerous Sundries' clerk Rolan. He will explain how Lorroakan is neglecting him in his search for the Nightsong. Player can ask Rolan to make a portal to Lorroakan.
- DEN_Prodigy_Sister.json: This occurs after the argument betwen Lia and Rolan. Lia is still stewing after the fight. Opportunity to get to know her better and understand the group dynamics.
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_RolanConclusion.json: Dialog after final confrontation with Rolan. Depending on whether he joined Nightsong team or not or if Lorroakan died or not different branches will be chosen.

context: Ide and Rolan have just had a falling-out: Rolan drank heavily (three bottles) and snapped at Ide, leaving Ide hurt, frustrated, and avoiding eye contact. Off-screen, Ide found an old, likely magical spellbook he had planned to give Rolan so the boy could learn instead of numbing himself, but Ide is now reluctant to hand it over. Rolan is an apprentice wizard haunted by his siblings’ capture by cultists—he actually protected the tieflings from Zevlor but feels like a failure and has been drinking. In this exchange the player can console Ide, press him for the book, or offer to deliver it — the player may end up taking the book to give to Rolan.
